name: The Smile
label: XL
lede: Thom Yorke and Jonny Greenwood of Radiohead, plus Tom Skinner of Sons of Kemet, turned up on a Glastonbury livestream in May 2021 as a band nobody knew existed. Their first album got Pitchfork's 8.6 and Best New Music.

eras.title: Thirty years of Radiohead, and the side jobs
eras.text: Yorke and Greenwood spend three decades inside Radiohead. Film scores, solo records and, for Skinner, a London jazz band of his own fill the gaps.

years.h: In Abingdon, a band called On A Friday starts rehearsing
years.p: [[Radiohead|a74b1b7f-71a5-4011-9441-d0b5e4122711]] are named for their rehearsal day until 1991, when they sign with EMI and change it.

years.cap: Thom Yorke with Radiohead at Nissan Pavilion
years.h: In Rainbows goes on sale at whatever price you pick
years.p: [[Radiohead|a74b1b7f-71a5-4011-9441-d0b5e4122711]] release the album digitally and let buyers set the price, Yorke's loudest argument yet with the record business.
years.xp:
Yorke has been blunt about labels. Wikipedia quotes him: "I like the people at our record company, but the time is at hand when you have to ask why anyone needs one."

The do-it-their-way habit carries over to The Smile, who release through XL and Self Help Tapes.

years.cap: Jonny Greenwood at Glastonbury, eight years before The Smile
years.src: Wikipedia: Tom Skinner · Wikipedia: Jonny Greenwood
years.h: Greenwood scores The Master with Skinner in the room
years.p: [[Tom Skinner|1d68b69c-ad5e-46c2-bede-4999dada10dd]] plays on [[Jonny Greenwood|e9fcfbbf-1743-4f73-8744-ada8da7394ea]]'s score for Paul Thomas Anderson's The Master, where the two first work together.
years.xp:
Greenwood has scored Anderson's films since There Will Be Blood (2007) and later collects Oscar nominations for Phantom Thread and The Power of the Dog.

Wikipedia names The Master as the connection that brings Skinner into The Smile years later.

years.src: Wikipedia: Sons of Kemet · Wikipedia: Tom Skinner
years.h: Skinner is drumming in Sons of Kemet when Burn comes out
years.p: Shabaka Hutchings' group, formed in London in 2011, puts out Burn on Naim with Skinner on drums.
years.xp:
Sons of Kemet use a saxophone, a tuba and two drummers. They win Best Jazz Act at the 2013 MOBO Awards, and their 2018 album Your Queen Is a Reptile is nominated for the Mercury Prize.

Skinner also runs Hello Skinny, which releases an album in 2012 and Watermelon Sun in 2017.

years.h: Yorke scores Suspiria, then goes solo again with Anima
years.p: [[Thom Yorke|8ed2e0b3-aa4c-4e13-bec3-dc7393ed4d6b]] scores the 2018 Suspiria remake without Nigel Godrich, then releases the solo album Anima in 2019.
years.xp:
Before that he'd led [[Atoms for Peace|9e299bee-d7e2-49f3-8cd7-d6b28ab204d1]] (Amok, 2013) and released Tomorrow's Modern Boxes through BitTorrent in 2014.

Wikipedia reports Anima is his first chart-topper on Billboard's Dance/Electronic chart.

eras.title: Three people who agree to say nothing
eras.text: Greenwood and Skinner trade ideas, Yorke joins a few months later, and lockdown does the rest. None of them talks about it.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Smile (band) · Wikipedia: Tom Skinner
years.h: Greenwood invites Skinner in, and Yorke follows within months
years.p: [[Jonny Greenwood|e9fcfbbf-1743-4f73-8744-ada8da7394ea]] asks [[Tom Skinner|1d68b69c-ad5e-46c2-bede-4999dada10dd]] to work on musical ideas. [[Thom Yorke|8ed2e0b3-aa4c-4e13-bec3-dc7393ed4d6b]] comes in a few months later.
years.xp:
The three agree not to give interviews about the project, so its first years are mostly off the record. Yorke later explained the name: "not the smile as in 'ahh', more the smile as in the guy who lies to you every day."

Wikipedia's Skinner page gives 2021 as the year he joined, which is when the band went public.

years.cap: The Smile at Magazine London, eight months after the Glastonbury debut
years.h: The Smile debut on the Glastonbury livestream with no warning
years.p: Live at Worthy Farm was filmed earlier that week. Across eight songs Yorke and Greenwood swap guitar, bass, Moog and Rhodes.
years.xp:
Some of the eight songs come from A Light for Attracting Attention, which nobody outside the band has heard yet.

Nigel Godrich, Radiohead's longtime producer, goes on to produce that debut album. Wikipedia says he cites the pandemic and Ed O'Brien's 2020 solo album Earth as factors in the project's emergence.

eras.title: A debut album, then the road
eras.text: The first album brings reviews and a place on Pitchfork's year-end list. The tour goes out, and two weeks in Skinner's other band calls it a day.

years.cap: The Smile in the round at Magazine London, January 30, 2022
years.h: Three nights in the round at Magazine London
years.p: The first live shows debut "Speech Bubbles", "A Hairdryer" and "Waving a White Flag". The band also covers Joe Jackson's "It's Different for Girls".
years.xp:
All three shows are livestreamed. They also play "Open the Floodgates", which Yorke first performed in 2010.

NME's James Balmont gives the run 4 out of 5. The Guardian's Kitty Empire also gives 4, writing that they are "most convincing when they stretch away from Radiohead"; her colleague Alexis Petridis gives 3 and calls it "intriguing rather than dazzling".

yt: "You Will Never Work in Television Again"
years.h: "You Will Never Work in Television Again" is the first single
years.p: It's out January 5, 2022, months after the Glastonbury livestream. The album is four months away.

years.src: Wikipedia: A Light for Attracting Attention · Pitchfork: The 50 Best Albums of 2022 · Pitchfork: The Smile review
years.h: A Light for Attracting Attention earns Best New Music
years.p: Pitchfork gives it 8.6 and ranks it No. 21 of 2022; Metacritic scores it 86.
years.xp:
It's recorded in London with Godrich during 2020-21. Yorke sings from home over streaming software during lockdown, fitting sessions around his children's school day. The cover is a gouache painting by Yorke and Stanley Donwood, done in Yorke's garden shed.

Pitchfork's Ryan Dombal calls it "instantly, unmistakably the best album yet by a Radiohead side project". It goes out digitally on May 13 and physically on June 17, and reaches No. 5 on the UK chart.

years.cap: The Smile at the Roundhouse, London, May 30, 2022
years.h: The first tour starts in Europe and crosses to North America
years.p: A July 2022 set at Montreux Jazz Festival is later released as a live album on December 14.
years.xp: Saxophonist Robert Stillman joins them for some songs. The setlists mix new material with Yorke's 2009 single "FeelingPulledApartByHorses".

years.cap: Skinner at the Roundhouse, London, May 30, 2022
years.h: Sons of Kemet close the chapter, two weeks into the tour
years.p: Skinner's jazz band stops "for the foreseeable future".

eras.title: A new producer, two more albums, one hospital stay
eras.text: Sam Petts-Davies takes over production, Paul Thomas Anderson films the videos, and a second and third album come out of the same sessions.

years.h: Paul Thomas Anderson films the video for "Bending Hectic"
years.p: The first single from the second album is out June 20, 2023. The director of There Will Be Blood and Phantom Thread makes the videos.

years.cap: The Smile at All Points East, Victoria Park, London
years.h: Wall of Eyes swaps Godrich for Petts-Davies and adds an orchestra
years.p: Pitchfork gives it 8.5 and Metacritic 83. The London Contemporary Orchestra plays strings throughout.
years.xp:
It's recorded at Greenwood's Oxfordshire home studio and Abbey Road, starting in March 2023. It peaks at No. 3 in the UK, and Wikipedia reports it was the country's highest-selling vinyl in its release week.

Anderson directs the videos for "Wall of Eyes" and "Friend of a Friend". Listening parties at independent cinemas come on January 19.

years.h: Greenwood lands in hospital and the August tour dates go
years.p: [[Jonny Greenwood|e9fcfbbf-1743-4f73-8744-ada8da7394ea]] is hospitalised in July with a serious infection. The August leg of the European tour is cancelled.

years.cap: The Smile at All Points East, Victoria Park, London
years.p: Pitchfork gives it 8.0 and Metacritic 82. Weirdcore makes the glitchy videos for every single.
years.xp: Yorke says splitting the material into two albums was to do it justice and avoid burnout. "Bodies Laughing" was written more than twenty years earlier and left unfinished until now. The album peaks at No. 7 in the UK.

eras.title: Radiohead calls again
eras.text: Yorke and Greenwood go back to Radiohead for a European tour. The Smile hasn't been called off.

years.h: Yorke and Greenwood rejoin [[Radiohead|a74b1b7f-71a5-4011-9441-d0b5e4122711]] for a European tour
years.p: It's Radiohead's first tour in seven years, per Wikipedia.
